events.title: Constantius Gallus arrives at Antioch as Caesar of the East
events.description: Gallus, appointed Caesar by his cousin Constantius II at Sirmium in March, reached his capital Antioch. Around this time the Jews of Palestine revolted under Isaac of Diocaesarea, a rising that Gallus's general Ursicinus later put down.
events.html: Gallus, appointed Caesar by his cousin Constantius II at Sirmium in March, reached his capital Antioch. Around this time the Jews of Palestine revolted under Isaac of Diocaesarea, a rising that Gallus's general Ursicinus later put down.

events.title: Main dome of Hagia Sophia collapses
events.description: Weakened by earthquakes, the great dome of Justinian's cathedral fell. It was rebuilt taller and steeper by Isidore the Younger, and that dome, though repaired, still stands.
events.html: Weakened by earthquakes, the great dome of Justinian's cathedral fell. It was rebuilt taller and steeper by Isidore the Younger, and that dome, though repaired, still stands.

events.title: Seljuk Turks defeat Antioch and Edessa at the Battle of Harran
events.description: At Harran, the Seljuk emirs of Mosul and Mardin defeated the Crusader states of the Principality of Antioch and the County of Edessa. It marked a turning point against Frankish expansion, and the Turks regained territory earlier lost to Antioch.

events.title: Castile and Aragon begin the siege of Málaga
events.description: Forces of Castile and Aragon besieged Málaga, the Emirate of Granada's second largest city and its most important port. It held out until 18 August, and most of its surviving people were then enslaved or put to death.

events.title: Louis XIV opens a grand festival at Versailles
events.description: Louis XIV began 'The Pleasures of the Enchanted Island', a week of spectacles and plays including Molière's first Tartuffe. Versailles became the seat of court and government in 1682.

events.title: Bienville founds New Orleans, by tradition on this day
events.description: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville chose a crescent of high ground on the Mississippi for a new French post. The city became a meeting point of French, Spanish, African and American cultures.
events.html: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville chose a crescent of high ground on the Mississippi for a new French post. The city became a meeting point of French, Spanish, African and American cultures.

events.title: HMS Victory is launched at Chatham
events.description: The 100-gun first-rate HMS Victory was floated out of dry dock at Chatham. Forty years later she was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, and she survives at Portsmouth as the oldest commissioned warship.
events.html: The 100-gun first-rate HMS Victory was floated out of dry dock at Chatham. Forty years later she was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, and she survives at Portsmouth as the oldest commissioned warship.

events.title: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is first performed in Vienna
events.description: Beethoven's Ninth, with its choral setting of Schiller's 'Ode to Joy', premiered at the Kärntnertortheater. The composer, almost entirely deaf, had to be turned to see the audience's applause.

events.title: German U-boat sinks the liner Lusitania
events.description: U-20 torpedoed the Cunard liner off southern Ireland, sinking her in 18 minutes with the loss of 1,198 lives, 128 of them American. Outrage in the US turned opinion sharply against Germany.

events.title: Germany signs its unconditional surrender at Reims
events.description: General Alfred Jodl signed the surrender at Eisenhower's headquarters, to take effect the next night. A second signing in Berlin followed at Soviet insistence.
